site.name: Pennsylvania Mine
overview: The Pennsylvania Mine is a historic hard-rock mine complex on the south side of Peru Creek near Montezuma. U.S. Geological Survey reporting identifies it as one of the most productive mines in the Montezuma quadrangle.

The vein was discovered in 1879, production peaked around 1893, and the property continued operating through difficult periods that closed many neighboring mines. The site is also important to modern water-quality work because mine drainage contributes acidic, metal-rich water to Peru Creek.

timeline.text: The Pennsylvania vein was discovered south of Decatur in the Peru Creek mining area.
The mine reached the height of its historic production and continued operating through the lean years that followed the silver panic.
The consolidated Pennsylvania property continued intermittent production of gold, silver, lead, copper, and zinc ores.
USGS studies of Peru Creek document acidic, metal-rich drainage from the Pennsylvania Mine and evaluate its contribution to downstream metal loading.

moreHistory: Historic USGS reporting records the Pennsylvania as one of the most productive properties in the Montezuma quadrangle.
Multiple mine levels, portals, waste dumps, timber remains, and the lower processing area preserve the layout of a substantial mountain mining complex.
